Chapter 3: The Work of a Medium—Bridging Two Worlds
Becoming a medium isn’t something you usually see coming. It feels more like a calling that shows up out of nowhere, shaking up your life in ways you never expected. And for those who find themselves in this role, the journey is honestly both thrilling and a little intimidating. There’s a real sense of responsibility here—delivering messages from the other side isn’t something you take lightly. Each interaction becomes this careful dance, honoring the spirit world while holding space for the emotions of the living.
Now, connecting with the other side might seem mysterious from the outside, but the process is actually more down-to-earth than you’d think. It starts with quieting your mind—setting aside your own worries and really listening. The messages that come through aren’t usually loud or dramatic. More often, they show up as quick flashes: maybe an image, a random word, or a feeling that just doesn’t quite fit. The real challenge? Trusting those impressions, even when they don’t make sense right away.
I remember a session with a woman who’d lost her sister. Out of nowhere, I felt a strong urge to mention a particular song. Honestly, I wasn’t sure why. But I decided to go with it. Her eyes filled with tears as she told me—that song was their childhood anthem, a private joke just for the two of them. In that moment, the room felt charged with connection. The message wasn’t about the past or the future. It was about the bond between two souls that simply refuses to fade.
You see, mediumship isn’t about predicting what’s coming or solving unsolvable mysteries. It’s about bringing comfort. Offering validation to people who are grieving. Most of the messages are simple—maybe a reminder to release guilt, or just reassurance that a loved one is at peace. Sometimes, it’s just a gentle nudge to help someone move forward. The goal isn’t to amaze or impress. It’s to heal.
Of course, there are challenges. Skepticism is always lurking—whether it’s from others or even from yourself. Some days, the messages are fuzzy or the emotions in the room feel overwhelming. It’s easy to doubt. But over and over, the details that come through—names, dates, private stories—are things I couldn’t possibly know on my own. And for the people receiving those messages, it’s deeply humbling. Sometimes, it’s even transformative.
Take the example of a man who came in after suddenly losing his wife. He walked in with this careful mix of hope and skepticism. He wanted to believe, but he was afraid of getting his hopes up. As I started sharing what I was picking up—a favorite flower, a spot they’d vacationed together, a phrase only the two of them used—something shifted. The skepticism melted away. The messages weren’t over-the-top, but they were deeply personal. By the end, he found a sense of peace he hadn’t felt since she was gone.
Mediumship isn’t a show. It’s a sacred trust. Every session is different, shaped by the people and the spirits involved. There aren’t any guarantees, no surefire formulas. The only thing that stays the same is the desire to help—to bring comfort and healing where it’s needed most.
Over time, mediums start to recognize the signs that a spirit is nearby. Maybe there’s a chill in the air, a tingling sensation, or a sudden wave of emotion that just seems to come out of nowhere. These are hints that the other side is reaching out. The process isn’t always easy, and there are moments of doubt and frustration. But the rewards? They’re incredible. Watching someone light up when they hear from a loved one—it’s a powerful reminder of the connections that matter most.
At the end of the day, being a medium isn’t about proving there’s an afterlife. It’s about reminding people that love endures. The bonds we share don’t just disappear. For those who are open to it, the experience can truly change your life. The other side is closer than you might think, always ready to offer comfort, guidance, and hope.
